content: Now that Lean core has the defProp linter (which does very similar things), shall we remove the defLemma linter as essentially duplicate? The same applies to checkUnivs.

In a similar vein, mathlib has a dupNamespace linter which

  • is a syntax linter, i.e. offers immediate feedback,
  • will check for any repeated namespace (e.g. Foo.Bar.Foo.Bar.baz will finally be linted; mathlib had about 45 such instances),
  • and also checks auto-generated declarations (so no regressions here).

Would a PR upstreaming this to batteries be welcome?
Yes. Three separate PRs, please!
batteries#1863 removes the defLemma linter
batteries#1864 removes the checkUnivs linter

For the dupNamespace linter, it's probably best to wait for #39793 (which supports checking for non-consecutive duplicates) to get merged. It has been maintainer merged, so hopefully that will happen soon.
Next question: what's the right process to create adaptation branches? Should I manually bump batteries once both PRs have landed?
Do you have write access to mathlib4-nightly-testing?

I do - would you like me to prepare building adaptation branches there?
Update: I have pushed a fixup commit to the corresponding nightly-testing branches.
Now opened as #40820 resp. #40821.
Wonderful! I normally add the blocked-by-batt-PR tag until the batteries PR is merged. See, for example, #35104 for my typical template.
Do pay attention to the bullet point steps.
Thanks, added that to each PR.
Was the simpVarHead linter also already removed?
Indeed, let me also make a PR for that.
batteries#1866 removes the simpVarHead linter
By the way, #40821 is ready for review now. @Jovan Gerbscheid maybe?
cc @Kim Morrison @Bryan Gin-ge Chen Could you fast track #40821? It's currently blocking the Mathlib test in Batteries.

Michael Rothgang said:

For the dupNamespace linter, it's probably best to wait for #39793 (which supports checking for non-consecutive duplicates) to get merged. It has been maintainer merged, so hopefully that will happen soon.

Hmm, I presume it would be worth also improving the core dupNamespace linter so that it also checks for non-consecutive repeats.
I'm happy to submit a PR to Lean core with the analogous improvement. Would you like me to?
That would be fantastic, thanks!

@Michael Rothgang I actually made the PR myself (lean4#14249), as I wanted to make the non-consecutive repeated usage of namespace components optional and controllable via an appropriate option. Projects might opt-in for consecutive checking, but it will be disabled by default.
Are there really cases where users want to have names with duplicate components in the namespace?

I think there are lots of cases where you might want this. In lean4#14072 I added modules Init.Data.Float.Model.Float and Init.Data.Float.Model.Float32. In this case these modules don't actually contain names with duplicate namespace components, but it's not so hard to imagine cases where you would want such names. If, ten years ago, mathlib had decided to call the top-level category theory folder Category instead of CategoryTheory, then possibly we would have lots of Category.Category in the library now. The linter makes sense for mathlib as it happens to exist today, and every library which finds it helpful should feel free to enable it, but I don't think it makes sense as a linter that is enabled by default.
Given that the linter itself is off by default, can consecutiveOnly be false by default?

Wojciech Różowski said:

Michael Rothgang I actually made the PR myself (lean4#14249), as I wanted to make the non-consecutive repeated usage of namespace components optional and controllable via an appropriate option. Projects might opt-in for consecutive checking, but it will be disabled by default.

Thanks! I left a minor comment on the PR.

Non-consecutive repetitions are perhaps rare in Mathlib, but they are not so uncommon in the greater Lean universe. Consider this concrete-ish scenario: Char.Ascii.Char is the (protected!?) subtype of Char consisting only of ASCII characters.
